items.title: L’école de Tivaouane: Un creuset de savoir en Afrique de l’Ouest
items.description: Tivaouane est devenue, sous l’impulsion de Seydi El Hadji Malick Sy, un pôle intellectuel relié aux grands centres du savoir musulman. Une dynamique qui a façonné l’identité cosmopolite de la Tijâniyya. Fondée par Seydi El Hadji Malick Sy au début du XXe siècle, l’école de Tivaouane a dépassé sa vocation de simple lieu d’enseignement religieux. Véritable foyer de formation intellectuelle et spirituelle, elle a façonné des générations de mouqadams (érudits), favorisé le brassage des peuples et jeté les bases du rayonnement international de la Tijâniyya. Mieux, elle a joué un rôle déterminant dans la construction d’un cosmopolitisme religieux, lequel continue d’inspirer les Tidianes. Disciple et non moins professeur d’anglais, Pape Amadou Sall voit l’école de Tivaouane comme un haut lieu du savoir et de la culture. Elle est, rappelle-t-il, une institution qui a formé d’éminents maîtres de la voie tidiane, les muqaddams, chargés de diffuser l’enseignement de Seydi El Hadji Malick Sy. Selon lui, cette école a, très tôt, concilié tradition et modernité. Pape Amadou Sall souligne également que l’historien David Robinson considère comme un accomplissement majeur de Maodo le fait d’avoir amené l’administration coloniale française à distinguer les Tidianes wolofs des Tidianes toucouleurs au début du XXe siècle. Le sociologue des religions Dr Cheikh Tidiane Mbaye voit dans la Tivaouane de Mame Maodo un véritable hub intellectuel en Afrique de l’Ouest. Des érudits issus de différentes régions y convergeaient pour approfondir leurs connaissances religieuses, renforçant ainsi le prestige de la cité religieuse et le rayonnement international de la Tijâniyya. Pour lui, cette vocation historique mérite aujourd’hui d’être ravivée par le développement de l’enseignement supérieur, de la recherche scientifique ainsi que du tourisme religieux et intellectuel. Seydi El Hadji Malick Sy avait une idée claire de sa stratégie pédagogique. Le guide religieux avait mis en place un système fondé sur une logique de centralisation, de décentralisation puis de recentralisation, explique Mouhamadou Mounirou Sy. « Les universités populaires de Ndiarndé, Diacksao et Tivaouane accueillaient des centaines de disciples, principalement des jeunes, qui recevaient une solide formation de base. Une fois instruits, ils retournaient dans leurs localités pour transmettre les enseignements reçus selon la même méthode », explique-t-il. Tivaouane a toujours demeuré le centre névralgique de ce vaste réseau de diffusion du savoir. Centralisation, décentralisation puis recentralisation L’école de Mame Maodo a aussi un « caractère profondément inclusif ». « Sans distinction d’origine, de fortune ou de rang social, tous les disciples étaient traités sur un pied d’égalité. Cette organisation favorisait une véritable fraternité entre les différentes communautés, renforcée par les liens matrimoniaux tissés entre les familles », souligne-t-il. Le cosmopolitisme tidiane est né dans la cour même de Seydi El Hadji Malick Sy avant de s’étendre progressivement à l’ensemble du territoire sénégalais, estime Mouhamadou Mounirou Sy. Cette lecture rejoint celle du professeur Bakary Sambe. Avant l’installation de Maodo, Tivaouane n’était qu’une modeste bourgade du Cayor. En quelques années, le guide religieux la transforma en une cité reliée aux grands centres culturels et spirituels du monde musulman, de Fès au Caire, du Liban à l’Arabie Saoudite. « Les relations entretenues avec la Zawiya-mère de Fès, les ijâzât reçues de savants marocains ainsi que les échanges qui se poursuivront après sa disparition témoignent de cette ouverture internationale », explique-t-il. Pour Bakary Sambe, le cosmopolitisme de Tivaouane ne relève donc pas d’un phénomène récent. Il constitue l’un des fondements mêmes de l’œuvre d’El Hadji Malick Sy. Aujourd’hui encore, signale-t-il, les dahiras et zawiyas implantés par la diaspora prolongent cet héritage. Aliou DIOUF

items.title: Atiku defends new subsidy model, accuses Tinubu of economic arson
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on Friday mounted a robust defence of his newly unveiled petroleum-sector intervention model, accusing President Bola Tinubu of economic arson, vandalism and propaganda in his condemnation of the proposal. He insisted that the president has mistaken Nigerians’ capacity to endure suffering for evidence that his economic policies are working. In a statement issued by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the African Democratic Congress ADC Presidential Candidate said there was an almost comical audacity in Tinubu calling anyone economically ignorant after presiding over an economy where government revenues have ballooned while citizens’ purchasing power has collapsed. Shaibu quoted Atiku as saying: “If economic ignorance had a presidential seal, Tinubu and his family would be its official logo. Here is an administration that detonated simultaneous fuel-price, exchange-rate and cost-of-living shocks across a fragile economy, watched millions become poorer, and now struts around Abuja demanding applause for the wreckage. “That is not reform. It is economic arson followed by propaganda about the ashes. “Tinubu’s courtiers may clap because Federation Account Allocation Committee FAAC allocations have increased, but hungry Nigerians cannot boil FAAC figures for dinner. Businesses cannot power factories with presidential speeches, workers cannot pay transport fares with macroeconomic grammar, and parents cannot settle school fees with statistics manufactured for State House applause. “A government that grows richer while its citizens grow poorer is not reforming an economy. It is extracting from its people. “Tinubu should therefore spare Nigerians the economics lecture. A man who set the house on fire cannot ridicule another man for redesigning the fire extinguisher.” Defending the substance of his proposed model against Tinubu’s dismissal, Atiku said: “Tinubu and his gang of jesters should acquaint themselves with elementary economics before accusing anyone of ignorance. Economic prescriptions respond to prevailing conditions. Even a first-year economics student understands ceteris paribus — other things being equal. “But other things are no longer equal in Tinubu’s Nigeria. “Apparently fresh from a bowl of amala, Tinubu mounted the podium at Eagle Square and casually declared that ‘subsidy is gone’ without a credible transition plan or adequate protection against the inflationary consequences. “Those three words were not economic policy. They were economic vandalism by presidential fiat. “Petrol prices exploded. Transportation and production costs followed. The naira depreciated sharply. Food prices soared. Businesses buckled and household purchasing power was decimated. “Having destroyed the economic assumptions upon which previous prescriptions rested, Tinubu’s propagandists now accuse Atiku of inconsistency for responding to the disaster they created. “That is not inconsistency. That is economics. Only incompetence insists on yesterday’s prescription after today’s conditions have changed.” Atiku clarified that his proposal was not a call for the return of the old subsidy arrangement, but a targeted, capped, budgeted, time-bound and independently audited production-support mechanism tied to domestic production and protected against arbitrage. “The difference is simple: Tinubu pronounced first and searched for a plan afterwards. Atiku studied the consequences and produced a solution”, the statement noted. He also queried the President’s claim that subsidy removal had benefited states through improved FAAC allocations, saying: “Now that Tinubu tells Nigerians that one of the great achievements of subsidy removal is that states which previously struggled to pay salaries now receive larger FAAC allocations, he must realise that this argument is economically shallow and, worse still, an admission of developmental failure. “You do not build a federation by impoverishing citizens so that Abuja can send bigger cheques to governors. That is robbing households to subsidise governments. “If the price Nigerians must pay for governors to meet their basic obligations is crushing transport costs, diminished purchasing power, food inflation and deepening poverty, then Tinubu has merely transferred solvency from the kitchen tables of ordinary families to government treasuries. “Worse still, this FAAC bonanza creates the wrong incentives. States should develop competitive economies, attract investment, exploit their comparative advantages, broaden their productive tax bases and create wealth. Instead, Tinubu is deepening an Abuja dependency economy where governors can wait every month for increasingly fat allocations from the centre. Why undertake difficult reforms, industrialise or expand productive capacity when Abuja provides an ever-growing monthly cheque? That is not fiscal federalism. It is fiscal sedation and rascality. “There is no economic morality in making a market woman poorer so that a governor can receive a bigger allocation. There is no developmental wisdom in emptying household pockets merely to fatten government accounts while Nigerians still confront bad roads, inadequate hospitals, failing schools and unemployment. “Tinubu did not solve the structural weakness of the states. He simply threw more money at it and sent the bill to Nigerians”, he declared. Atiku also demanded that the Presidency reconcile outstanding fiscal questions with the same urgency it deployed against his proposal: “And since the Presidency has suddenly discovered the speed to respond to Atiku, let it show similar enthusiasm in explaining the approximately ₦30 trillion in Federation Account revenues, deductions, savings and transfers that Atiku has demanded be reconciled, as well as the ₦12.8 trillion Service-Wide Vote in the 2026 budget. “You cannot scream ‘hoax’ at a proposal designed to ease hardship and suddenly become deaf and dumb when confronted with questions of fiscal opacity, alleged budget padding and questionable expenditure. “If Tinubu can mobilise an army of propagandists to attack Atiku within hours, surely he can find one accountant to explain his books”, he stated. The post Atiku defends new subsidy model, accuses Tinubu of economic arson appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘Hundred promises, not one fulfilled’ – Bella reacts to Sheggz breakup
items.description: Big Brother Naija star Bella Okagbue has broken her silence on her breakup with fellow reality TV star, Sheggz, saying she eventually chose to speak after watching people tell her story for her. Bella, who addressed the development in a series of posts on her Instagram Story, said she initially remained silent because she believed some aspects of their relationship were better kept private. “For the past few days, I have watched people tell my story for me. I stayed silent because I believed some things deserved to remain private, but my silence should never be mistaken for guilt,” she wrote. The reality TV star said she genuinely loved Sheggz and defended their relationship because she believed in it at the time. According to her, she also chose to give him a second chance because she believed people could grow and change. “I loved genuinely. I defended the relationship because I believed in it at the time, and I chose to give someone I loved a second chance because I believe people can grow and change. That was my choice, and I own it,” she said. Bella, however, noted that believing someone could change did not mean she was obligated to wait indefinitely for that change. She also suggested that the version of Sheggz known publicly was different from the person she experienced privately. “The person everyone experiences publicly isn’t always the person you experience privately,” she stated. Addressing discussions surrounding marriage and Sheggz’s plans to marry her, Bella said wanting marriage with someone she loved should not be interpreted as desperation. She maintained that knowing when to walk away from a relationship was an important decision, adding that a marriage proposal or ring could not solve problems within a relationship. “On marriage and the ring, let me be clear: wanting marriage with someone you love is not desperation. Knowing when not to marry them is discernment. Sometimes, it takes more courage to walk away than to stay,” Bella wrote. “A ring doesn’t fix what made a relationship impossible.” Bella further revealed that she had heard different versions of events circulating online, some of which she said did not reflect her experience. “There are versions of events circulating that do not reflect my experience, just as there are parts of my experience I have chosen not to discuss publicly yet. Those are mine to tell, when appropriate,” she said. The reality TV star also claimed she had given the relationship love, loyalty and an opportunity for change, but eventually reached a point where she could no longer continue. “I gave love a chance. I gave change a chance. I gave loyalty in abundance,” she wrote. “But even loyalty has an expiry date when trust, respect and peace can no longer coexist with it.” Bella said she did not regret giving the relationship another chance, but had now reached a point where she knew trying again was no longer the answer. “I don’t regret being the woman who chose to try again. I respect the woman I am today enough to know when trying again is no longer the answer,” she said. She concluded by saying she had chosen herself and would make a different choice regardless of the consequences. “So today, I choose myself. I choose differently, regardless of what comes with it,” Bella added. Vanguard News The post ‘Hundred promises, not one fulfilled’ – Bella reacts to Sheggz breakup appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nadra makes Proof of Life certificate free for pensioners, expands access points
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra) has made the Proof of Life Certificate (PoLC) free for pensioners and expanded access to the document through multiple channels across the country, including the PakID mobile app, registration centres, union councils and e-Sahulat franchises. The initiative, launched on Friday, was taken on the special directives of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in coordination with the Ministry of Interior, Ministry of Defence, Controller General of Accounts (CGA) and Military Accountant General (MAG). A PoLC is an official document that verifies that a pensioner is alive. According to Nadra, the easiest option is the PakID mobile application, through which eligible pensioners can obtain the certificate digitally from home. An immediate family member can also obtain the certificate on a pensioner’s behalf through their own PakID account, subject to the prescribed identity verification process. For those preferring assisted services, the certificate is available free of charge at more than 5,000 e-Sahulat franchises. It is also available at more than 988 Nadra Registration Centres and 500 Union Councils, where pensioners are given preferential service without having to wait in the regular queue. For pensioners unable to reach a service point, Nadra said the facility is also available through mobile registration vans, biker services and ManPack registration services , which cater to citizens with limited mobility or access. The PoLC service is part of a wider reform under which Nadra has established a National Pensioners Register. In Phase I, pensioners administered by CGA and MAG have been brought onto the register to provide an authenticated digital reference for identity and life-status verification. Nadra said it would now provide daily digital intimation to the concerned pension controllers in case of the death of a primary or secondary pensioner reported through the Death Notification Tool by a health facility or registered through the Civil Registration Management System (CRMS). Similarly, changes affecting the entitlement of secondary or family pensioners, including their age and marital status, will be communicated daily to pension controllers where such changes are reflected in Nadra’s records. Decisions regarding the continuation, alteration or cessation of a pension will remain with the competent pension authority under the applicable rules. A separate verification service has also been made available to banks, allowing authorised banks to check a pensioner’s proof-of-life status directly through the National Pensioners Register. Nadra said this would provide a digital channel for pension disbursement and reduce reliance on repeated physical or paper-based verification. Nadra said the register was planned to be expanded in the next phase to include pensioners from other federal and provincial government organisations, public-sector bodies and private institutions after agreements and institutional arrangements were concluded. The authority said the integrated system was intended to ease proof-of-life requirements for pensioners while enabling pension controllers and banks to work with more up-to-date and verified information.

items.title: Industrie automobile : le Maroc continue d’attirer les équipementiers chinois
items.description: Un nouveau fabricant chinois de composants automobiles s’apprête à installer sa première usine hors d’Asie au Maroc. Ce projet illustre la montée en puissance du Royaume dans les chaînes de valeur mondiales de l’automobile, portée par la proximité du marché européen, l’écosystème industriel local et la présence des grands constructeurs internationaux. Le Maroc renforce son positionnement dans les chaînes de valeur automobiles mondiales. Un fabricant chinois spécialisé dans les systèmes de commande automobile a confirmé son intention d’implanter une unité de production dans le Royaume, qui deviendrait sa première base industrielle hors d’Asie. Une nouvelle illustration de l’attractivité croissante du Maroc auprès des équipementiers internationaux cherchant à se rapprocher du marché européen. Selon une note d’analyse publiée début mai par le courtier chinois Dongxing Securities, cette future filiale marocaine devrait servir de principal hub de production international du groupe. Le projet, évoqué pour la première fois en 2025, pourrait mobiliser jusqu’à 20 millions de dollars en financement en capital. L’entreprise, cotée à Shanghai, produit notamment des leviers de vitesse électroniques, des pédales d’accélérateur ainsi que différents systèmes de câblage automobile. Elle fournit déjà plusieurs grands constructeurs internationaux, dont Renault et Stellantis, avec lesquels elle a réalisé ses premières livraisons à l’étranger en 2025. Le choix du Maroc s’inscrit dans une logique industrielle désormais bien établie chez les fournisseurs asiatiques du secteur automobile. La proximité géographique avec l’Europe, les accords de libre-échange avec l’Union européenne, les coûts compétitifs ainsi que la présence des usines Renault à Tanger et Stellantis à Kénitra renforcent l’attractivité du Royaume pour les sous-traitants cherchant à rapprocher leur production de leurs clients. Le rapport de Dongxing Securities souligne également les avantages liés au foncier, à la fiscalité et au coût du travail, dans un contexte où les équipementiers automobiles subissent une pression croissante sur leurs marges. Pour les fournisseurs opérant avec les grands groupes européens, produire au Maroc permet de réduire les coûts logistiques tout en sécurisant les chaînes d’approvisionnement. L’entreprise chinoise reste encore dans une phase préparatoire. Les procédures administratives et réglementaires liées à la création de la filiale n’ont pas encore été finalisées, tandis que l’enregistrement officiel de la société au Maroc n’a pas encore démarré, selon son rapport annuel 2025. Cette implantation intervient alors que le groupe accélère son internationalisation. Jusqu’à récemment, l’entreprise opérait exclusivement sur le marché chinois. En 2025, elle a toutefois enregistré ses premiers revenus à l’international, pour un montant de 7,24 millions de yuans (environ 1 million de dollars américains). Une étape encore modeste, mais symbolique dans sa stratégie d’expansion. Sur le plan financier, le groupe affiche des indicateurs solides. Son chiffre d’affaires a progressé de plus de 8% en 2025 pour atteindre 1,58 milliard de yuans, tandis que son bénéfice net a augmenté de plus de 13%. Les ventes de certains équipements électroniques destinés aux véhicules ont enregistré des hausses à deux chiffres, portées par la transformation technologique du secteur automobile. L’arrivée de ce nouvel acteur s’inscrit dans une dynamique plus large d’investissements chinois dans l’industrie automobile marocaine. Plusieurs groupes ont récemment annoncé des projets industriels majeurs dans le Royaume, couvrant aussi bien les alliages électroniques que les batteries, les matériaux stratégiques ou encore les pneumatiques. The post Industrie automobile : le Maroc continue d’attirer les équipementiers chinois appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

Burkina : Bientôt l’opération « Zéro poulailler vide » pour renforcer la production avicole nationale
items.description: Le Gouvernement burkinabè à travers le Ministère de l'Agriculture, de l'Eau, des Ressources Animales et Halieutiques s'apprête à mettre en œuvre dans les jours qui suivent l'opération « Zéro poulailler vide ». Cette initiative que s'inscrit dans la mise en œuvre de l'Offensive Agropastorale Hydraulique et halieutique, vise à accroître les productions nationales et à renforcer la souveraineté alimentaire. Elle a pour objectif d'améliorer la disponibilité des produits aviaires sur le marché national afin de répondre aux besoins croissants des populations. L'information a été donnée au cours d'une conférence de presse, ce vendredi 21 août 2026 à Ouagadougou. L'opération « zéro poulailler vide » va consistera à doter 500 bénéficiaires disposant déjà d'un cadre approprié pour l'aviculture d'un kit d'élevage avicole. Le Kit a une valeur estimée de 2 140 000 FCFA et 1 335 000 FOFA respectivement pour l'élevage moderne et l'élevage traditionnel de reproduction. Le kit de l'élevage moderne est composé de 1000 poussins de race ou souche local amélioré d'une valeur de 750 000 FCFA, 3 350 kilogrammes d'aliments couvrant entièrement la phase d'élevage pour un montant de 1 240 000 FCFA. A cela s'ajoute des produits vétérinaires et des prestations de suivi sanitaire d'une valeur estimée à 150 000 FCFA. Pour le Kit de l'élevage traditionnel, les bénéficiaires auront 100 volailles adultes dont 10 coqs et 90 poules pour une valeur de 600 000 FCFA, 2 000 kilogrammes d'aliment couvrant 6 mois d'élevage pour un montant de 720 000 FCFA. items.title: Burkina: opération « Zéro poulailler vide »
items.description: Le ministère burkinabè en charge des Ressources animales a annoncé, ce vendredi 21 août 2026 face à la presse à Ouagadougou, le lancement prochain de l'opération « Zéro poulailler vide » pour faire face aux difficultés rencontrées par les aviculteurs. Face aux difficultés rencontrées par les aviculteurs, qui ont entraîné une baisse de la production avicole, le ministère de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques a animé une conférence de presse, ce vendredi 21 août 2026, en vue de relancer le secteur à travers une opération dénommée « Zéro poulailler vide ». D'un coût de plus d'un milliard de francs CFA, cette opération vise à soutenir les promoteurs de fermes avicoles afin de contribuer à la relance de la production avicole et à la redynamisation du secteur. Un lien sera disponible et à partir de lundi, les bénéficiaires pourront s'inscrire. Au total, ce sont 500 bénéficiaires qui vont être retenus. Le ministère a élaboré un engagement que chaque bénéficiaire devra signer et respecter sous peine de sanction. Des détails à venir …. Par Bernard BOUGOUM L’article Burkina: opération « Zéro poulailler vide » est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: La Russie frappe à nouveau l'industrie militaire ukrainienne, Zelensky se plaint d'une guerre toujours plus coûteuse
items.description: Les forces russes ont mene des frappes de drones contre une entreprise industrielle situee a Brovary, dans la region de Kiev, a annonce, ce 21 août, le ministere russe de la Defense. Le site etait lie aux forces armees ukrainiennes et avait ete entierement mis hors service pour une duree indeterminee a la suite de l'attaque. Sur fond de poursuite du conflit, Volodymyr Zelensky, de son cote, a insiste sur les difficultes financieres croissantes de l'Ukraine. Le « president ukrainien » a notamment estime que Kiev devrait avant tout parvenir a trouver les ressources necessaires pour poursuivre son effort militaire. Toujours d'apres lui, l'Ukraine doit non seulement renforcer sa defense face aux capacites employees par la Russie, mais egalement agir de maniere « plus active », ce qui exige des financements supplementaires. « La guerre est devenue plus coûteuse, c'est un fait. Il faut davantage de ressources, le deficit est de plus en plus important », a-t-il declare. Kouleba ne voit plus de marge pour accroître l'aide occidentale Les possibilites de trouver ces ressources aupres des partenaires etrangers pourraient cependant etre limitees. Dmytro Kouleba, ancien ministre ukrainien des Affaires etrangeres, a souligne que l'Ukraine avait desormais atteint le plafond du soutien international et qu'il ne voyait actuellement aucune source susceptible de permettre une augmentation significative de l'aide. Selon lui, Kiev beneficie deja depuis cinq ans d'un soutien considerable, representant des dizaines de milliards d'euros et de dollars. Dans les circonstances actuelles, l'ancien chef de la diplomatie ukrainienne a donc juge peu probable que les partenaires occidentaux puissent aller beaucoup plus loin. Kouleba a explique cette situation par la configuration politique actuelle en Europe et par les difficultes economiques rencontrees par plusieurs acteurs majeurs. Il a egalement fait savoir que les etats-Unis ne souhaitaient pas financer davantage l'Ukraine. Toujours selon lui, Kiev doit par consequent se montrer particulierement prudent lorsqu'il evalue le niveau de soutien sur lequel il pourra compter a l'avenir. L'ancien ministre a egalement evoque les tensions a l'interieur du pays. Il a averti que la colere suscitee par la situation actuelle avait deja atteint un niveau tres eleve dans la societe ukrainienne et prevenu qu'elle pourrait encore fortement progresser pendant l'hiver.

items.title: I’ll consider review — Oppong Nkrumah hints at next move after Supreme Court dismisses injunction
items.description: Ofoase-Ayirebi Member of Parliament Kojo Oppong Nkrumah has hinted at seeking a review of the Supreme Court’s decision dismissing his application to halt selected criminal trials during the legal vacation. Justice Gabriel Pwamang, sitting as a single judge of the Supreme Court, dismissed Mr Oppong Nkrumah’s interlocutory injunction application on Friday, August 21. The application sought to stop selected criminal trials from proceeding during the legal vacation, which runs from August 1 to September 30. Oppong Nkrumah said the court made what he described as “very interesting pronouncements” in its ruling, including an observation that some cases had been treated differently during the legal vacation. Speaking to journalists after Friday’s proceedings, he said the legal team would first study the certified true copy of the ruling before deciding on the next course of action. “So, the court has dismissed our injunction application. But in the ruling, some very interesting pronouncements have been made. For the first time, the court has admitted that some cases have been treated differently. Those are the words of the judge,” he said. Mr Oppong Nkrumah said the judge acknowledged that certain cases had been treated differently and expedited during the legal vacation. He said the judge, however, concluded that the differential treatment did not amount to a violation of the constitutional provisions relied on in the case. “He doesn’t say so. But then he proceeds to say that in his opinion that will not amount to a violation of the constitutional articles that we have raised in this particular matter. And that he thinks that that will even be in the interest of the accused persons,” Mr Oppong Nkrumah said. The MP said the legal team had requested a certified true copy of the ruling to enable them to examine the court’s reasoning in detail. “We’ve asked for a certified copy so that we can peruse it some more and then on the advice of counsel we’ll take the next steps,” he said. Asked whether he was considering an application for review, Mr Oppong Nkrumah responded: “Very much so, very much so, but we’ll consider it.” He then referred the matter to his lawyer, Frank Davies, for further comment. Earlier, Mr Davies said the legal team accepted the court’s decision and would study the full written ruling before advising their client. “We will abide by the ruling of the court for now,” he said. Mr Davies said the lawyers would examine the certified copy of the judgment before determining what further legal action, if any, should be taken. The dismissal means the affected trials can continue while the substantive suit challenging the constitutionality of the Chief Justice’s administrative warrants remains pending. The cases include the trial of former National Signals Bureau Director-General Kwabena Adu-Boahene and his wife, as well as former NAFCO Chief Executive Officer Hanan Abdul-Wahab, among others. Mr Oppong Nkrumah is expected to make a decision on a possible review after studying the certified true copy of Friday’s ruling with his legal team.

items.title: El Niño pourrait devenir l’un des épisodes climatiques les plus intenses jamais observés
items.description: Le prochain épisode d’El Niño pourrait atteindre une intensité exceptionnelle, avec une hausse de la température de surface du Pacifique dépassant les 3 °C dans une zone de référence, selon des experts du Met Office britannique. Ce phénomène pourrait provoquer des sécheresses, des inondations et des tempêtes dans plusieurs régions du monde. Le phénomène climatique El Niño suscite déjà l’inquiétude des météorologues. Selon Adam Scaife, responsable des prévisions de long terme au Met Office, l’épisode attendu pourrait être « le plus intense depuis plus d’un siècle ». El Niño se produit lorsque les températures de surface de l’océan deviennent exceptionnellement élevées dans les régions centrale et orientale du Pacifique équatorial. Le phénomène revient généralement tous les deux à sept ans et peut perturber les conditions météorologiques dans de nombreuses régions du globe. D’après les prévisions citées par Le Parisien, le prochain épisode pourrait dépasser 3 °C de hausse de la température de surface de la mer dans la zone de référence du Pacifique. Pour les experts, un tel niveau serait inédit dans les relevés climatiques modernes. Le climatologue Zeke Hausfather estime également que les prévisions deviennent de plus en plus préoccupantes. Selon lui, plusieurs mois sont encore nécessaires avant que le phénomène atteigne son plein développement, mais les indications actuelles renforcent l’hypothèse d’un événement exceptionnel, qui pourrait même être le plus puissant depuis plusieurs siècles. Des conséquences à l’échelle mondiale Les effets d’El Niño sont généralement particulièrement marqués dans les régions tropicales. Le phénomène peut notamment provoquer des sécheresses importantes en Amérique du Sud et dans l’ouest du Pacifique, tandis que d’autres régions peuvent connaître des précipitations beaucoup plus importantes. L’Europe pourrait également être touchée. Adam Scaife indique que les premiers signes laissent envisager une intensification des précipitations et des tempêtes au Royaume-Uni et dans le nord-ouest de l’Europe à partir de novembre. L’impact pourrait surtout se faire sentir en 2027. Selon les prévisions citées, l’intensité du prochain El Niño pourrait contribuer à faire de cette année l’une des plus chaudes jamais enregistrées, voire la plus chaude. Les scientifiques restent toutefois prudents concernant le lien entre le changement climatique et l’intensité d’El Niño. L’Organisation météorologique mondiale rappelle qu’il n’existe actuellement « aucune preuve que le changement climatique augmente la fréquence ou l’intensité des événements El Niño ». En revanche, le phénomène intervient désormais dans un contexte de réchauffement global, ce qui peut accentuer les conséquences des événements météorologiques extrêmes. Face à ces risques, l’Organisation météorologique mondiale insiste sur l’importance des prévisions saisonnières et des systèmes d’alerte précoce, indispensables pour permettre aux populations et aux autorités de se préparer aux conséquences potentielles de cet épisode climatique exceptionnel. items.description: Au cœur des Alpes suisses, les plus grandes fortunes preparent deja leurs biens a affronter le pire. Dans le massif du Brünig, des bunkers destines a abriter des objets de valeur en cas de catastrophe sont en cours de construction a plus de 100 metres sous terre, rapporte le 20 août Bild . Derriere ce projet hors norme se trouve la societe Brünig Mega Safe AG. Les travaux ont debute en janvier 2026. Selon l'entreprise, les principaux travaux dans la zone de haute securite sont desormais termines. La prochaine etape prevoit la construction, a partir de janvier, d'un portail donnant acces aux espaces de stockage. Les premiers coffres pourraient etre operationnels en 2028. Le prix est a la hauteur de la clientele visee : la location d'un espace pour 99 ans peut atteindre un million d'euros. Les premiers contrats ont d'ailleurs deja ete signes. Brünig Mega Safe AG promet un niveau de protection comparable a celui des reserves de la Banque nationale suisse. Les proprietaires pourront y mettre a l'abri pratiquement tout ce qu'ils souhaitent, y compris des voitures. Seuls les stupefiants et les explosifs seront interdits. Pour penetrer dans les installations, il faudra franchir plusieurs niveaux de controle. Particularite, les droits de stockage accordes pour plusieurs decennies seront inscrits au registre foncier, donnant ainsi a ces espaces un statut juridique proche de celui d'un bien immobilier. Le sous-sol helvetique se prete particulierement bien a ce type de projets. En Suisse, de nombreux massifs montagneux sont divises en parcelles appartenant a des communes, des corporations ou des particuliers. D'anciens tunnels militaires ont ainsi deja ete reconvertis en caves a fromage, champignonnieres, stands de tir, centres de donnees ou entrepots. Toutefois, les Alpes ne sont pas le seul endroit ou les plus riches cherchent a se preparer aux scenarios les plus sombres. Un refuge capable de fonctionner presque seul Le 6 août, le Financial Times a revele qu'un groupe d'entrepreneurs du secteur technologique amenageait en Argentine un immense ranch autonome destine a servir de refuge en cas de guerre nucleaire, de catastrophe climatique ou d'effondrement economique. Baptise « Wamani », le domaine se trouve dans la province de Mendoza, au pied des Andes, a environ une heure de route de la localite la plus proche. Il s'etend sur 32 000 hectares. Au cours des deux dernieres annees, des maisons prefabriquees, des domes geodesiques et une piste d'atterrissage y ont ete construits. Le projet est porte par l'entrepreneur argentino-espagnol du secteur informatique Martin Varsavsky. L'objectif est de rendre Wamani aussi independant que possible du monde exterieur. Les bâtiments doivent etre equipes de panneaux solaires, tandis que le betail sera eleve sur place. Les entrepreneurs envisagent egalement d'acheter une parcelle supplementaire afin d'y cultiver des produits agricoles. Leur preparation ne s'arrete pas aux besoins materiels. Ils etudient egalement la possibilite de telecharger a l'avance de grands modeles de langage sur des ordinateurs alimentes par l'energie solaire. Selon Varsavsky, si les serveurs mondiaux tombaient en panne, ce dispositif pourrait disposer d'une sorte d'« Internet limite » fonctionnant de maniere autonome.

items.title: Bodies of two hikers missing for decades found after Swiss glacier melts
items.description: The bodies of two Belgian men who went missing in the Swiss Alps in 1992 have been discovered after being exposed by the melting of a glacier, police have said. A hiker discovered the bodies on 26 July on the Trift Glacier, south of the Swiss city of Lucerne, officials said. DNA analysis later confirmed them to be those of two mountaineers who went missing 34 years ago near the Weissmies mountain, police said. They were aged 39 and 41 at the time of their disappearance. Many scientists attribute a rapid retreat in Switzerland’s glaciers – which shrunk by a quarter in the decade to 2025, according to Glacier Monitoring in Switzerland (Glamos) – to climate change. Police in Switzerland’s Valais region said in a statement that they had organised a recovery operation following the discovery of the two men’s bodies and transferred them to a hospital in the canton’s capital, Sion, for identification. Peaking at over 4,000 metres, the Weissmies mountain – which the two men went missing in the vicinity of – is a popular mountaineering spot in the Saas Valley. Regional officials maintain a database of missing people dating back to 1925. The majority of people on it disappeared in the moutains, or in rivers and other bodies of water, police said. The force noted that this was not the first time that the melting of glaciers had exposed the remains of people who had gone missing several decades prior. In 2023, human remains found on a glacier close to Switzerland’s famed Matterhorn were confirmed to be those of a German climber who had been missing since 1986. The rate of glacier shrinkage has been increasing globally since the 1990s and at a particularly accelerated rate since 2000, according to the European Commission’s monitoring body Copernicus. This melting has been particularly pronounced in Switzerland. Data from Glamos reported a further glacier reduction of 3% across 2025, following record years of ice loss in 2022 and 2023. The upward trend in global average temperatures has brought unseasonably warm weather to Switzerland’s higher altitudes, and a reduction in snow has imperilled some of its ski resorts and competitions.

items.title: NSMQ 2026: North East Region denied one-eighth stage as Kumasi High kicks out Nalerigu
items.description: Nalerigu SHS and Jachie Pramso SHS have been sent packing from the National Science and Maths Quiz after falling short in a three-school preliminary contest at the SMS Auditorium, with Nalerigu’s return to the national stage ending at the first hurdle. ‎ ‎For Nalerigu, the result is particularly painful. The school had broken a three-year drought to return to the national stage after qualifying from the North East Region, but its 34 points were not enough to keep its campaign alive. Its elimination closes the chapter for the North East Region in this contest, with the region now without a school to compete for one of the 49 places in the One-Eighth Stage. ‎ ‎Kumasi High School on the other hand, took control of the contest from the opening round and finished on 45 points. It started with 14 points, moved to 20 in Round Two and reached 29 after Round Three. A strong fourth round lifted its score to 42, before three more points in the final round confirmed its position at the top. The result gives Kumasi High another opportunity to build on its past record in the competition. The school won the 2024 Ashanti Regional Championship after defeating Opoku Ware School and reached the One-Eighth Stage in 2025, where its run ended against Swedru Secondary School. Jachie Pramso finished on 30 points, four points behind Nalerigu, bringing another preliminary-stage outing to an end. ‎ ‎Kumasi High now moves into the next stage of the competition with the chance to improve on last year’s run. For Nalerigu, however, a long-awaited return to the national stage has ended sooner than hoped, while Jachie Pramso will also have to wait for another opportunity next year. items.title: Useless Column: ‘Weytin do Akosua?’
items.description: Did you know that a single fin whale releases 250 gallons of urine into the sea every single day? If you didn’t know, please you too urinate and let’s measure and see something. I recently visited an African country. It is a Francophone country. As soon as the police saw me, I heard them saying, ‘This man is from Ghana; they urinate everywhere!’ Jesus! Oh! The way I felt bad er. Not a good way to brand ourselves, but is it not true? Ah! I am here arguing with myself. Hmmm! Thank God another weekend is here again, and we at the ‘Useless Column’ are smiling it off before frowned faces kill us. Frowned faces have never solved any problem; they only worsen problems! Here, nothing is in any particular order. Basaaaaa… chakaaaaa… Hahaha! So the crescendo made the build-up exciting and full of fun. The climax gets it to the peak, and then it frowns, bowing its head in shame, awaiting consequences; these may be positive or negative. In the walls of a medical facility, negative is good news, while positive can only be good news if it is a pregnancy test. No bi so? Na sooooo…hahahahaha, but I am sad and really confused. But before I go on, I am a conservative consumer of many things, including fuel. Is fuel in the category of ‘consummables’? Just ‘asking’ to be sure. No vex me. Ah! I recently decided to buy fuel somewhere and see the difference. It was a journey from Akatsi to Accra. I decided to fill my tank at Sogakope, and the nearest filling station was STAR OIL. I gave it a try. The long and short of this non-fa is that since July 25, 2026, I have been buying my fuel from STAR OIL- a real value for money. I am impressed! All my ten cars, including my two V8’s and 2 Toyota Viz. I am rich! Ajeeeeeiiiii! So you believe I have ten cars? Hahaa! This is the problem I create for myself, and when some people start giving me pressure for Momo, I start complaining and refusing to pick up their calls. I don’t have anything yet; always bragging about nothing. What is this? Let me delete these lies from this ‘useless article.’ They say, ‘Let the weak say I am strong.’ It’s in the Bible. You naaa, you know you are weak but just say you are strong. Anyway, my latest problem is new. I am trying not to think about it, but the moment I stop to think about it, the more I think about it. I am to attend her funeral this weekend, but I am sad not because she’s passed but…heyi hmmm! The last time I met her was two years ago at a wedding outside Accra. When I asked what happened to her, I was told she has not been feeling well for some time now. The one who broke the news to me was not professional at all; he was so graphical in his konkonsa that I started to be super worried. He said Akosua started growing lean and developed rashes all over her body. This part nearly made me faint. Then I asked what the doctors said was the cause. She said that information is not available, but he recalled that Akosua has been visiting the Fevers Unit before the distin. I screamed in my head and heart, “Jesus! Jesus!! Jesus!!! You see how we abuse the name ‘Jesus’ and, more so, His blood! ‘Blood of Jesus, consume them.’ Consume who? I wonder if there is any blood left for us to solve more serious problems. We abuse things too much. The slightest thing, we would scream ‘Jesus’ especially when we are about to commit a crime or have finished committing a crime; we scream Jesus. Anyway, He has forgiven us. So I proceeded to ask what the other symptoms were, and my konkonsa friend mentioned that ‘when the thing started, Akosua started experiencing fever after some flu-like symptoms. It was in an air-conditioned restaurant where I was holding a chilled beer, but drinking it felt hot in my throat. He also mentioned that according to the medical doctors, not everyone will have the same symptoms, as it depends on the person and what stage of the disease they are in; he believed that Akosua’s condition was spiritual. I took comfort in that; after all, spiritual problems are not sexually transmitted. You see why I said the problem no dey finish? Because as I was happy that Akosua joined her ancestors as a result of a certain spirit, at the same time, I was worried that it was linked to the symptoms of a certain disease. What did you mean by the ‘disease’? I queried quickly in my head, but this guy will not stop his death sentence narrative to me. As if he was sent by the devil to come and torture my life with life-threatening news, he went ahead to suggest that some of the signs and symptoms of the disease are rashes, night sweats, fever, chills, muscle aches, sore throat, fatigue, swollen lymph nodes, mouth ulcers, and plenty of things. This guy must be sent to come and finish me before my time. I thought he would leave it at that point where he said Akosua might have passed on as a result of a spirit; he is now giving me ideas as to what I might have contracted too, possibly. Moments after listening to him, I suddenly started experiencing some of the symptoms, including heavy sweats and diarrhea. Alla! Akosua journeys on to her ancestors tomorrow. Memories of what happened two years ago started playing in my mind all because of ‘What if? Men would often say, ‘Life is short,’ but when the fear of that deadly virus hits us, we begin to see spinning around almost immediately with so many things running through our minds. It was only a night of, ‘My dear, come and lie on my laps since you are scared of mosquitoes.’ It was at a wedding we attended together outside Accra. It was drizzling, and Akosua and I decided to go to a movie house to watch movies while we wait for the wedding bus to pick us up later in the evening. In fact, the movies ended up watching us. Who watches movies at movie houses? Please give me way; let me pass er. I made her sit on my laps and my 5 th limb got provoked, and we ended up doing the ‘needful.’ She didn’t want it but that was not my problem; it was her problem, which I solved anyway. It was nice and short. Within one and a half minutes, we were done with no protection. I wore my useless boxer shorts and started thinking, ‘What if she gets pregnant or anything else?’ As for pregnancy, that’s not much of a problem. I can hide her and the baby from my wife, but what if it is that virus? Here comes the screaming of His name again for the wrong reasons: ‘Jesus’! Thankfully, it was not about pregnancy but the ‘Bra Panyin Danger virus.’ The name sounds nice—virus. I don’t know why the deadliest diseases have the nicest names. Osteoporosis, diabetes, arthritis, pneumonia, meningitis, hypertension, apoplexy, and angina (this one sounds like something sweet that must not be eaten with the mouth, though some of us use our mouths and heads to enter when we want to…hahaha). Now I have to live with the fear. I am still afraid to go and do the test to confirm. To confirm exactly what? What if? Ei! See you next week, and remember sweet things are dangerous. The sweeter, the more dangerous, as ‘sin fascinates and assassinates’!

items.title: Context Matters: Understanding the Tony Elumelu First-Name Debate – Afanyi Dadzie writes
items.description: Yesterday, a video went viral in which Nigerian billionaire and Group Chairman of UBA, Tony Elumelu, inadvertently drew the attention of a young female mentee at a public event to the fact that she could not simply refer to him by his first name. The lady subsequently corrected herself. The incident has, understandably, generated widespread debate. In the midst of the conversation, someone dug up a video of an interview Tony Elumelu gave in the UK, specifically at Stanford Business School. In that video, the female host addressed him simply as “Tony”. Because I had shared the initial video, someone tagged me in the Stanford video and asked for my opinion. I think this Stanford video actually helps us put the matter in proper perspective and reinforces the argument some of us have been making in support of Tony Elumelu. There is something called: high-context culture and low-context culture. African and Asian societies are largely considered high-context cultures, while Europe and many Western societies are generally regarded as low-context cultures. If you move through life without understanding cultural nuances in different places and spaces, you will constantly offend people without even realising it. For instance, in Ghana and many parts of Africa, it is considered disrespectful to interact with people using your left hand as a gesture. In Europe and elsewhere, you can do the same thing and nobody may even notice or criticise you. Comparing the Nigerian and UK Videos My argument is that this whole conversation about using first names is ultimately about context, environment, philosophy, and familiarity. I have worked for 21 years, but Multimedia Group was the first place where I encountered an HR policy that was very clear about the use of first names. I struggled with it, especially when it came to top managers. The first day I met the Group CEO, Kwasi Twum, at work, he insisted that if I didn’t call him Kwasi, he wouldn’t respond to me. It was a huge struggle for me, but I had to adjust. Why was it a struggle? Because it wasn’t the cultural norm in Ghana, and I had never experienced that philosophy in any corporate environment before. But take this from me: the same Kwasi Twum may not necessarily find it pleasant if he leaves that MGL corporate environment, goes somewhere else, and a young man of my age who doesn’t know him personally simply calls him by his first name. What has changed? Not necessarily his philosophy. The environment has changed. The familiarity is absent. And the context is different. The Stanford scenario was clearly an interview within a university setting, with an audience seated and a much older person interviewing Tony Elumelu. Secondly, a business school environment is, in many ways, similar to a corporate environment where people engage with a senior business executive professionally. Most importantly, this was not an African cultural setting. It was in the West, where the use of first names is generally normalised, including in many professional and institutional settings. But in an African setting, where a young mentee who is also a stranger gets up and calls a man of Tony Elumelu’s pedigree and age simply by his first name, outside a corporate environment where that has been established as the norm, I can understand why it may be considered off and contrary to protocol and etiquette. This is why we need to understand the nuances and appreciate the context. And frankly, I like the fact that we now have these two situations to compare because they demonstrate the point perfectly. Is it true that in Europe and the West, calling people by their first names is generally more common, with less emphasis on age and social status? Yes. Is that the norm within African culture? No. Does that make one culture or philosophy better than the other? Absolutely not. It simply means that cultures have different social codes, and sometimes the same behaviour can be perfectly acceptable in one environment and considered disrespectful in another. Context matters.

items.title: What’s Happening to the WNBA Isn’t Normal
items.description: Let’s start with the good: The WNBA is more popular than ever. During the offseason, the league and the WNBA Players Association reached a landmark collective-bargaining agreement resulting in a 400 percent increase, on average, in player salaries . The average franchise valuation has soared 59 percent in the past year ; the Golden State Valkyries were appraised at a league-high $850 million. Between now and 2030, the WNBA will add three new teams, in Cleveland, Detroit, and Philadelphia. And the WNBA saw a 44 percent jump in ratings for this year’s All-Star Game—which, for the first time ever, hosted more in-person fans than the NBA’s . Yet this success has come amid unprecedented controversy. In early July, a group of 11 Republican lawmakers sent a letter to Cathy Engelbert, the WNBA’s commissioner, demanding that she be held accountable for not adequately addressing “repeated acts of unnecessary physical hostility and violence” on the court against the Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark, who has emerged as one of the league’s most popular players. The letter also suggested that these acts may be “racially motivated” against Clark, who is white, and called for the Department of Justice to investigate. And right before the All-Star Game, Clark’s teammate Sophie Cunningham told ESPN , “I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men,” which immediately became a massive talking point around and outside the league. Shortly thereafter, multiple rallies sprung up in support of Cunningham; Celeste Keaton, a co-owner of the Seattle Storm, was suspended after verbally confronting a pair of teenage fans during a game who were holding signs supporting Cunningham. The discussions surrounding Cunningham and Clark have different origins; nonetheless, because they play together, their respective dramas have snowballed into one messy dispute that now envelops the league. Engelbert has certainly guided the league into its most financially stable era, but this is a complicated crossroads requiring delicate steering. Even if the WNBA isn’t in immediate danger of losing popularity, culture wars can be exhausting over time. And because its explosive success is the very thing attracting many of its critics, a narrative course correction may not be so simple. But the league needs to protect its players, and be careful not to kowtow too much to its critics. Managing the WNBA responsibly is especially challenging in this political and media environment. As Media Matters for America recently noted , Fox News has dedicated at least 206 segments to the WNBA since late June, most of which revolved around racial issues or the inclusion of trans athletes in the league. It’s difficult to refocus attention when a major news network isn’t letting up. Much of what’s happening now began when Clark entered the league, in 2024. In a short time, her tenure has helped the WNBA transform financially and receive more mainstream attention. But Clark’s stratospheric popularity has been complicated to manage. By keeping her views private, she’s become a blank slate for anyone’s cause. Though she has never publicly acknowledged her own political leanings, prominent conservatives have wielded Clark against her own league to advance MAGA’s racial grievances. And whenever a perception emerges that Clark is being treated unfairly by her peers, the backlash is outsize. In June, the Phoenix Mercury forward Alyssa Thomas was suspended after hitting Clark in the throat during a game, one of the incidents prompting the letter from the Republican lawmakers. It was a bad play, but aggressive physical contact is an inevitable part of sports . Yet it was treated as an outlier: Thomas, who is Black, told reporters that after her play with Clark went viral, she received death threats and was called racial slurs . The heated environment can be seen as part of a larger outcry. The league is about 70 percent Black, and anywhere from 25 to 35 percent queer; historically, its players have embraced progressive issues. In 2016, the Minnesota Lynx wore T-shirts calling for justice and accountability following the police-related deaths of Philando Castile and Alton Sterling . A few years later, Senator Kelly Loeffler of Georgia, a Republican, wrote a letter to Engelbert criticizing the league’s support of the Black Lives Matter movement. In response, players backed Raphael Warnock, who eventually won the seat from Loeffler in the 2020 election. This history has made the WNBA low-hanging fruit for MAGA figures, whether politicians or commentators, who use it to score cheap points with their base. Critics lacking a serious investment in women’s basketball can conveniently swoop in to recite their spiel, and pay no attention to the sport itself. When the league was less popular, its players may have been freer to express their opinions without blowback. Perhaps that’s no longer possible. During All-Star weekend, I spoke with the Lynx’s rookie sensation, Olivia Miles, who talked about the difficulty of using the league as a platform for other issues, given the current attention. “Learning how to navigate that through sports is not an easy thing to do, because everyone is watching us at all times,” she said. “There’s so many things that are said and done and criticized.” The freedom to voice one’s politics goes both ways, and in Cunningham, conservative critics have a figure whose beliefs explicitly align with theirs on one particular topic. In the ESPN profile, she characterized her politics as “very much in the middle.” But her actions have drawn polarized attention. In Minneapolis, Cunningham took pictures with the former college swimmer Riley Gaines, who for years has advocated to keep transgender women out of women’s sports, and whose activism has been far more explicitly partisan. (Gaines has said the Biden administration “pushed radical gender ideology every chance it got,” and campaigned for President Trump.) “I think it’s people just practicing their rights of freedom of speech and doing what other fans have been doing since the WNBA has started,” Cunningham told reporters of the rallies held in her support. “And so props to them, props to everyone who is able to be competent and be bold and courageous enough to speak their truths.” Now coaches and players are being peppered with questions about where they stand—even though the league has never had a trans-woman player. (Layshia Clarendon, who was the first WNBA player to undergo top surgery , identified as nonbinary and trans. They retired in 2024.) Clark, too, has been criticized for not backing Cunningham’s stance. Some, like the Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve, are choosing to do their own form of counterprotesting. Reeve wore a T-shirt during a recent game against the Fever that read Trans Kids Belong ; ahead of the game, she defended trans rights to the media . “I’ve chosen to listen to transgender families, and what I know is exclusion is not the answer,” she said. This is a snapshot of the current WNBA experience—unprecedented growth and great basketball at risk of being swallowed up by the same culture wars plaguing the broader political landscape. Nearly every day brings some new development conflating the conflicts. Last week, the former NBA players Royce White and Enes Kanter Freedom announced their intentions to identify as transgender in order to play in the WNBA . (It’s highly unlikely they’ll be allowed in the league.) During a game, Cunningham received a hard foul ; the other player, the Chicago Sky’s DiJonai Carrington, was ejected and subsequently posted “WHITE PRIVILEGE” to social media. The implication, presumably, was that Carrington, who is Black, was more heavily penalized because of the perception that Cunningham, and by extension her image and outspokenness, needs to be protected. With the overall success of the league at stake, being dragged into the political fray may be a steep price to pay for visibility. Still, the players don’t seem ready to shut up and dribble. “I think it’s really important that we don’t lose something that’s a foundational truth in our league, to the growth,” Jonquel Jones, who plays center for the New York Liberty, told me during All-Star weekend. “There’s enough space where we can grow as a league but still continue to have our integrity and continue to operate in a certain type of way. I feel like we’re losing that a little bit.” [ Read: A brief exchange that shows the enormous difference between Trump and Obama ] Competitive friction is one thing—but all of the WNBA’s players, regardless of who they are and what they believe, are now being publicly harassed. Before the All-Star Game, members of the players’ union executive and justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion committees met with league officials to express their concerns about the escalation in abuse. Yet the players are, in many ways, subject to political dynamics outside their control. “We’ve experienced a lot of great changes, but the perspective I have, it really weighs heavily on—and I want to say this in a way that isn’t taken the wrong way—this isn’t a problem that was created by the players,” WNBA Players Association President Nneka Ogwumike told me. “So looking to us to always fix it is not the only way.” The question now is how the league can cool the rhetoric used around it. Clark, for example, has criticized the racism and misogyny that her fame has brought upon the WNBA, but that has done little to slow it down. When she was asked about the pregame demonstrations supporting Cunningham after a recent game against Minnesota, she opted for a generic, noncommittal answer . “I think it’s for leagues and the governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions, but our focus is on basketball,” she said. Perhaps she shouldn’t have to be more forceful—but soon enough, she may not have a choice. Meanwhile, Cunningham has taken a different approach. Detractors call her “MAGA Barbie,” a nickname she’s disavowed, although, at the very least, she’s played just enough footsie with MAGA to enrich her own personal brand. Nevertheless, she seems to recognize that things have gotten out of control: “I’m going to let people just do the speaking for themselves, but for me, I want to get back to basketball,” she said in early August . But how exactly can the league pivot back to basketball, especially during a time when outrage is so easily stoked? Last Wednesday, a task force of WNBA-team presidents and general managers met to discuss trans-athlete inclusion, as well as the abuse that many of their players have received. In a statement released after the meeting, the league denounced the outside criticism as “bad-faith efforts” that were meant to “demean or marginalize others.” The meeting didn’t result in any new eligibility guidelines regarding trans players, and it showed that the league is on the defensive—which won’t cut it. The WNBA doesn’t get the luxury of being conveniently neutral the way other leagues do, not when its Black and queer players remain easy targets. Yet while all of this has been going on, excellent basketball is still happening. The league hasn’t imploded. Clark and Cunningham are able to play without causing riots. Nobody’s taken the bait regarding White and Freedom’s trollish provocations. Perhaps the best thing the WNBA can do is stay firm in its own identity, even if a few brushfires get started in the process. A more visible commissioner with consistent messaging certainly could help. But all of this stems from the players feeling the freedom to express themselves—and, in turn, feeling confident in their capacity to navigate any criticism. In a way, the fuss around Clark and Cunningham shows that giving in to the social-media comments section isn’t the answer. The league needs to be who it is, and take whatever comes with it.

items.title: From ‘Indispensable’ Ally to Target of Annihilation
items.description: W hen the United States was looking for a way to talk to Iran about a nuclear deal more than a decade ago, it turned to Oman, asking the country to do something it had quietly done for years: make an impossible conversation possible. Because Washington and Tehran had no diplomatic relations, the U.S. felt that the most promising back channel to get a conversation started led through Muscat. Iran was skeptical but willing to sit down with U.S. officials, provided there was some very particular diplomatic choreography. At Tehran’s request, Oman’s government found a room with multiple doors, so that American and Iranian officials would not be seen entering together. Omani officials took the head of the table, to create the impression that it was more than a bilateral conversation. That session laid the groundwork for what ultimately became the 2015 nuclear pact. “Without Oman, I’m not sure there would be an Iran nuclear deal,” Jake Sullivan, one of the top U.S. officials involved in those talks, told me. But today, that pact lies in ruins. President Trump tore it up, then went to war with Iran. Oman has watched its standing with Washington collapse too. Earlier this week, Trump threatened to “bomb the shit” out of the sultanate unless it did what America demanded—adding another longtime ally to the list of countries he has threatened to attack. Oman, located on the southeastern edge of the Arabian Peninsula, is often overshadowed by its wealthier, more conspicuous neighbors, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, and by its more tumultuous neighbor, Yemen . Yet for decades, Oman punched above its weight diplomatically by serving as one of Washington’s most useful interlocutors in the Middle East, in part because it has maintained relationships with governments that Washington often cannot or will not talk to. Trump has accused the sultanate of undermining his efforts to strike a deal with Iran and end the war, which began at the end of February and are now in a stalemate . The Strait of Hormuz, which is central to the conflict with Tehran, is also at the center of Washington’s dispute with Oman. The maritime corridor used to carry one-fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied-natural-gas supplies before the U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran began and Tehran closed the strait to traffic through drone, small-boat, and mine attacks. Trump responded with a U.S. blockade, which remains in place even though the deadline for Washington and Tehran to reach an interim deal and set the stage for broader talks over Iran’s nuclear program expired earlier this week, showing no sign of a breakthrough. Oman and Iran border opposite sides of the strait; their respective territorial waters meet in the 21-mile-wide choke point. The two countries have been in talks in recent weeks to restore commercial ‌shipping, which has dwindled to a trickle. Both countries have floated the idea of a service fee for passage through the strait, but other Gulf nations have objected. Trump has wavered on the issue, though Secretary of State Marco Rubio has repeatedly said that the strait must return to being an open and free waterway. Trump has vowed to declare the strait a U.S. territory. He recently claimed that the strait was reopened and that mines and other hazards have been cleared. Shipping trackers continue to show a rate of passage dramatically below prewar levels. Omani officials insist that charging for passage is within the country’s legal rights. When asked on Monday in the Oval Office whether he was out of patience ​with Oman, Trump told ​reporters: “No, I don’t think ⁠they behaved very well, but we’d handle them very easily, just like we do other things.” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has separately threatened Oman with sanctions if Muscat facilitates fees for ships passing through the strait. A U.S. official familiar with the deliberations told me that the administration views Oman’s handling of the negotiations as “dishonorable,” accusing Omani intermediaries of publicly portraying the two sides as nearing an agreement while privately conveying proposals to U.S. officials that the latter viewed as unacceptable. The official also accused Oman of delivering false statements to the press, which Omani officials deny. But this much is clear: The role that Oman used to play for Washington as a useful regional intermediary is over—at least as long as Trump remains in office. T he president’s anger presents an unusually awkward problem for Washington and for Muscat. Oman is not some distant neutral country that wandered into an American dispute. It has spent decades deliberately cultivating its relationship with Washington. “Oman has decided its strategic importance is to be nonaligned the way Switzerland is nonaligned,” Jon Alterman, the chair in global security and geostrategy at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, told me. “It’s a relatively small, relatively poor place, surrounded by giants, and Oman has decided it will make itself indispensable to everyone—not because it helps everybody, but because it’s a place that can keep a secret and allows people to meet quietly and resolve conflicts.” [ Read: Trump’s new strategy of nothing ] Modern diplomatic relations between the United States and Oman date to 1972, but their history goes back much further. In 1833, President Andrew Jackson’s administration signed a Treaty of Amity and Commerce with Oman, then an important maritime power, as Washington sought to expand commercial ties in the region and protect American merchants operating in the Indian Ocean. An American consulate operated in Muscat from 1880 to 1915. In 1980, after the Iranian Revolution and the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, Oman became the first Persian Gulf state to officially grant the U.S. access to its military facilities. Oman doesn’t host a large, permanent American base like the Al Udeid Air Base, near Doha, the capital of Qatar. But Washington does have access to Omani military facilities and ports. In 2019, the two countries expanded that arrangement to include Duqm and Salalah, two key ports on the Arabian Sea, allowing American ships to operate and resupply outside the Gulf before entering the Strait of Hormuz. Oman has also spent decades pursuing a foreign policy designed to maintain relationships across the region’s fault lines. It has good relations with Iran, maintains a security partnership with the United States, and has kept channels open to the Houthis, an Iranian-backed militia in Yemen. It has also maintained contact with Israel. This is often described as Omani “neutrality,” though some of the sultanate’s regional neighbors believe that it favors Tehran. That has sometimes put Oman at odds with its fellow Gulf states, especially Saudi Arabia and the UAE, which view Iran as a major regional security threat. Oman declined to join the Saudi-led intervention in Yemen in 2015 and stayed out of the 2017 regional blockade of Qatar. Muscat also maintained channels to the Houthis, whom Riyadh and Abu Dhabi have long battled. One Saudi official I spoke with offered a skeptical assessment: “Oman’s definition of neutrality has been questionable.” Oman rejects the idea that its connections to Iran, including its economic relationship with and ties to the Houthis, amount to complicity. Instead, it casts its ties as a relationship of economic and regional importance. Oman serves as an economic lifeline and reexport hub for Iran, absorbing trade activity that previously passed through the UAE. (The UAE announced this week that it is stopping all trade and financial transactions with Tehran.) Iran, meanwhile, supplies Oman with agricultural products and heavy materials. A senior Omani diplomat I spoke with described neutrality as a practical necessity for a small state surrounded by larger powers. Oman, the official argued, gets criticized from all sides. “The Iranians will tell us, You’re being too soft on the West ,” the official told me, while Western governments accuse Oman of being too soft on Iran. “And the Houthis will tell us we’re being too nice to the Saudis, and the Saudis will tell us we’re being too nice to the Houthis. It just goes with the territory.” But Oman’s independence—its ability to talk to all sides, even if it irritates the others—is precisely what has made Muscat useful to successive American administrations. O man’s record as an intermediary is unusually long. The country has helped secure the release of American detainees held by Iran. It has also facilitated contacts involving Yemen. In early 2013, a small group of senior American officials quietly boarded a military plane bound for Oman. For years, John Kerry had been nurturing a diplomatic channel with Muscat, meeting secretly with Omani officials while he was chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee in hope of opening back-channel talks with Iran. As President Obama’s secretary of state, he gave the green light to dispatch top foreign-policy officials to Muscat, including then–Deputy Secretary of State William Burns and Sullivan, who was serving as national security adviser to then–Vice President Biden. Those talks helped form the basis for the 2013 interim nuclear agreement and, eventually, the 2015 Iran nuclear deal. During the Biden administration, Muscat hosted the U.S. special envoy for Yemen, Tim Lenderking, and brokered his first direct contacts and message exchanges with Houthi representatives. Oman “wanted peace in Yemen, and they were willing to travel to Sanaa to meet with the Houthis and pass messages to Houthi leadership and exert their influence where they could to help us achieve a durable peace,” Lenderking, who is now a principal at the Washington-based law firm Squire Patton Boggs, told me. In 2025, the Trump administration again turned to Oman to host negotiations with Iran. Trump subsequently thanked Sultan Haitham bin Tariq, the country’s leader, for Oman’s role. [ Read: The art of the giveaway ] In addition to serving as an intermediary, Oman offers Washington military access and a stable partner near one of the world’s most important maritime choke points; Oman gets a powerful security partner while preserving the freedom to maintain its own relationships. But that bargain hinges on Oman’s independence. Analysts told me that this is why the current rupture matters. If the U.S. wants Oman to function as an intermediary, it cannot simultaneously demand that Muscat adopt Washington’s preferred position toward Iran. The very quality that makes Oman useful—the ability to talk to everyone—can look like disloyalty. That old paradox has now become a crisis. Oman says that it is trying to fulfill its obligations under international law and keep commercial shipping moving, including through Omani territorial waters. The Omani diplomat told me that the country’s lawyers believe that maritime fees can be lawful under international practice and that Oman has no intention of doing anything illegal. Trump and his negotiators see the issue differently, particularly where any arrangement could give Iran greater control over shipping or legitimize Iranian fees in what Tehran could portray as a victory over its much more powerful nemesis. Other nations have stepped in to play crucial mediating roles in this conflict, thus far to no avail. But Muscat remains one of the few doors available to American negotiators. The difficult question now is whether Trump’s threats will finally slam it shut.

items.title: Algérie : une météorite martienne vieille de 1,273 milliard d’années révèle ses secrets sur la planète rouge
items.description: Une meteorite decouverte en 2019 dans le Sahara algerien pourrait apporter de nouvelles reponses sur l'histoire geologique de Mars. Baptisee Northwest Africa 13441 (NWA 13441), cette roche d'origine martienne a ete datee a environ 1,273 milliard d'annees, selon une etude publiee le 1er août dans la revue scientifique Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta . Cette decouverte est particulierement importante pour les planetologues. Les meteorites martiennes sont des fragments de la planete rouge projetes dans l'espace a la suite d'impacts, avant d'atteindre la Terre apres un voyage de plusieurs millions d'annees. Environ 400 meteorites martiennes ont jusqu'ici ete identifiees. La grande majorite appartient a la famille des shergottites, des roches magmatiques formees a partir de magma. Or, jusqu'a present, les shergottites etudiees etaient essentiellement âgees de moins de 600 millions d'annees ou d'environ 2,4 milliards d'annees. Il existait donc un « trou » important dans les connaissances, couvrant pres de deux milliards d'annees de l'histoire geologique de Mars. Une periode jusque-la largement inconnue NWA 13441 vient precisement combler une partie de cette lacune. Son âge de 1,273 milliard d'annees constitue le premier âge de ce type identifie pour une shergottite sur cette periode. « Les caracteristiques de cette meteorite etaient tout a fait surprenantes », a explique Ethan Baxter, professeur de sciences de la Terre et de l'environnement au Boston College et coauteur de l'etude. Selon lui, aucune autre meteorite martienne connue presentant des caracteristiques similaires n'avait jusqu'ici ete datee de 1,27 milliard d'annees. Les chercheurs ont notamment analyse les isotopes du neodyme, un element naturellement present dans les roches. Les resultats ont revele une particularite inattendue : la composition isotopique initiale de NWA 13441 correspond a celle du systeme solaire primitif, il y a environ 4,56 milliards d'annees. Cette signature est normalement associee aux chondrites, des meteorites constituees de materiaux n'ayant pas subi de fusion et considerees comme des vestiges des premiers temps du systeme solaire. Une partie des profondeurs de Mars resterait intacte La presence de cette signature dans une shergottite pourrait indiquer qu'une partie des regions profondes de Mars est relativement preservee depuis la formation de la planete. Mars s'est en effet forme tres rapidement, moins de cinq millions d'annees apres la naissance du systeme solaire. Contrairement a la Terre, la planete rouge ne possede pas de plaques tectoniques actives capables de recycler continuellement les materiaux de sa croûte et de son manteau. Cette absence de recyclage pourrait ainsi avoir permis a certains materiaux tres anciens de demeurer enfouis pendant des milliards d'annees avant d'etre finalement incorpores a la roche dont provient NWA 13441. La meteorite presente egalement une autre particularite : sa signature isotopique ne correspond pas exactement aux sources deja identifiees des shergottites. Les chercheurs envisagent donc l'existence d'un reservoir martien encore jamais echantillonne, situe entre les sources dites « enrichies » et « appauvries ». L'equipe scientifique poursuit desormais l'etude de l'echantillon en analysant d'autres systemes isotopiques. L'objectif est notamment de determiner comment cette roche se rattache aux autres meteorites martiennes et d'ameliorer la comprehension de l'evolution magmatique et volcanique de Mars. Le Sahara algerien, un terrain privilegie pour les meteorites Au-dela de son interet scientifique, l'histoire de NWA 13441 rappelle le role majeur du Sahara dans la decouverte de meteorites. Les vastes etendues desertiques constituent des terrains particulierement favorables a leur reperage : les roches sombres se distinguent facilement sur les surfaces sableuses et l'extreme aridite limite leur alteration. De nombreuses meteorites decouvertes dans le Sahara portent ainsi la designation « Afrique du Nord-Ouest », une nomenclature regionale utilisee pour cataloguer des fragments retrouves dans cette partie du continent.
